newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU postpones debate on tobacco subsidies.
newsitem.headline: EU postpones debate on tobacco subsidies.

text.p: The European Commission postponed on Wednesday a debate over whether the European Union should continue to subsidise tobacco farmers.

Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn had intended to ask his colleagues at their weekly meeting to phase out tobacco production subsidies on the grounds that they contradict the EU's efforts to discourage smoking.
But the EU executive postponed the discussion to next week after running out of time, Commission officials said.

Flynn's initiative is opposed by Agriculture Commissioner Franz Fischler, who argues that it would put about 135,000 farmers out of work without cutting tobacco consumption since most tobacco in the EU is imported.
He favours instead targeting subsidies on higher-qualilty tobacco.
The EU spends about one billion Ecus ($1.26 billion) a year on tobacco subsidies, with Italy and Greece the main beneficiaries.
Flynn argues that the average quality of EU tobacco is so low that its commercial value is only one-fifth of the subsidies used to grow it.
